findings.title: canManage() grants manage access to callers that only hold the VIEW scope on groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) succeeds, i.e. when the caller has either the 'view' or the 'manage' scope on the all-groups ('Groups') resource. canManage() is what GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses (auth.groups().requireManage()), and canList()/canView() delegate to it indirectly as well. As a result an admin who was only granted 'view' on all groups can create top-level groups in the realm. The per-group variant canManage(GroupModel) correctly checks only MANAGE; the realm-wide variant should do the same (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)). The interface Javadoc added in this PR for canManage() even documents this escalation ('VIEW or MANAGE groups'), so the doc must be corrected together with the code.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns resource UUIDs instead of group IDs and never finds per-group resources
findings.body: In V2 a group's authorization resource is created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with name = group.getId() and no type is set (resourceStore.create(...) only; compare GroupPermissions.initialize which calls setType("Group")). This method does resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups", ...), which therefore only ever matches the 'Groups' all-groups resource itself (the only one given a type in init()). For each hit it calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) — passing the resource UUID where a group ID (resource name) is expected, so findByName fails and the check silently falls back to the all-groups resource — and then adds groupResource.getId() (the resource UUID, not a group ID) to the result. Consequences: (1) an admin with VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS on individual groups gets an empty set, so UsersResource.getUsersCount(...) (which passes this set to getUsersCount(realm, groupIds)) returns 0 even though the admin can see members; (2) an admin with VIEW_MEMBERS on the all-groups resource gets a set containing the resource UUID, which UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource store as UserModel.GROUPS and pass to searchForUserStream, so the user search is restricted to a non-existent group and returns no users. The user search tests only pass because, when the set is empty, the stream falls back to per-user canView filtering. Fix: use groupResource.getName() both for the permission check and for the returned IDs, and ensure resources created for Groups get a type (or iterate differently).

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc references the wrong predicate
findings.body: The new Javadoc on requireManageMembers(GroupModel) says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. The implementations (GroupPermissions.requireManageMembers) actually check canManageMembers(GroupModel), which is a different permission (manage-members scope vs manage-membership scope). The doc should reference canManageMembers.

findings.title: getResourceName() does not handle the new Groups resource type
findings.body: getResourceName resolves friendly names only for the Users resource type ('All users' / username). For the newly added Groups type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is never set for resources created by getOrCreateResource (they are created with only a name equal to the group ID), so callers (e.g. policy/permission representations shown in the admin console) will get null or the raw group ID for group resources, and nothing equivalent to 'All users' for the 'Groups' all-resource. A GROUPS branch returning e.g. 'All groups' / group path or name should be added alongside the Users branch.

findings.title: switch on resourceType throws NullPointerException for a null resource type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource now does `switch (resourceType)` on a String. If resourceType is null (e.g. a ScopePermissionRepresentation with resources but no resourceType reaching this path), the switch throws a NullPointerException instead of the previous controlled IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object ..."). A null guard before the switch (or including it in the default branch message) keeps the error reporting consistent.
